baseBranch: legion/LEGION-631 (sjawhar/legion#1843, open, head 57077591); the daemon created legion/LEGION-663 at main's tip bff9f310 (#1869), so the planner's chain is a conflict-free merge commit of both (9121e30e) carrying this handoff; the pull request opens with --base legion/LEGION-631 and is retargeted to main by a forward merge when #1843 merges, where the contract number is re-checked against main
concerns: A deployment row judged by any failing live session: one tree whose repository disables a tool opens the row deployment-wide until that process relaunches; the per-claim view and the row detail name the culprit (spec wording; architect may prefer per-claim only)
The MCP check opens a second short-lived client per configured server at every session boot (a stdio server is spawned once more for ~0.5 s); a single-client server reads open with its error
End-to-end rows (github, dispatch-envoy-tools, web-search) report a service outage as a gap for the sessions that booted during it; it heals at that claim's next boot
promptAgents is the union over every role's prompts, so every pod is held to every role's agents

The retarget to main after #1843 squash-merges will conflict in legion.ts, claim-session.ts, daemon-client.ts, legion-api.ts, version.go, claims.go, the state fixtures and docs/kubernetes.md; the branch's version is the resolution, and contract 19 may need renumbering if main took it first
The merger must not publish READY while the pull request's base is legion/LEGION-631; it reports to the architect instead
Stage 4b's negative control writes .omp/config.yml into tree 2's workspace (tree 2 never opens a pull request); the checkpoint removes it and its cleanup trap removes it on abort
designSummary: Every workflow session (pod container or tmux pane) measures the six live capabilities inside Oh My Pi at boot, after claims/register and before claims/ready, with the in-process API the boot gate's load probe already uses (discoverAgents, runSearchQuery, discoverMCPServers + waitForPendingConnections, discoverExtensionPaths + loadSkills, getActiveTools for the ten envoy_* tools plus a real `dispatch read`, `gh api user`); each check 8 s, the report 10 s, failures become ok:false with the fact. ReadyRequest gains `capabilities` {measuredAt, elapsedMs, rows[{name, ok, detail}]}, RegisterResponse gains `promptAgents` (the union of the role prompts' task agents), contract 18 -> 19, `live` leaves CapabilityState (an unreported live row is `unchecked` with its ruling; the four rows without one get dispatch://LEGION-663). The daemon never refuses a report (drops unknown rows, truncates, marks missing rows open), persists it in claim_capabilities (migration 0036) and keeps the latest per claim in supervision memory; a live row is judged over claims that are ready/working/idle whose report incarnation equals the claim's current one: open when any fails (naming pod/pane, role, issue, fact), present when none fails and one proved it; open live rows reach the log at report time, Open()/openCapabilities, and legion state, with no capabilities.decided line. ClaimView gains a compact `capabilities` view. Stage 4b gets real bun stdio MCP servers in the fixture, a `full-agent` checkpoint and a `full-agent-negative` one (a workspace .omp/config.yml turning web_search off plus a planner relaunch).

findings.answer: Measured: at the cut-off Oh My Pi logs 'handler timed out' and stops waiting while the handler's promise keeps running (claims/ready and the legion tool registration still complete). The measurement runs concurrently with the jj attribution and the Envoy role claim after register, each check 8 s, the whole report 10 s, boot today 1-3 s, so the handler stays far inside 30 s; the report stays on ready as the spec says.
findings.finding: The report sits on the boot's critical path inside a 30 s session_start handler whose cut-off behaviour is unstated

findings.answer: Measured in an rpc session with pi-envoy loaded first: all ten envoy_* names are in getActiveTools() (and getAllTools()), and /opt/legion/pi-envoy/bin is on PATH; the ten names are pinned by a test against envoy-client's envoyToolSpecs.
findings.finding: dispatch-envoy-tools reads getActiveTools(), but extension tools may only be in getAllTools()

findings.answer: Measured in this pod with the operator overlay present: a workspace .omp/config.yml with web_search: {enabled: false} removes web_search from getActiveTools() and getAllTools(); the workspace survives a container restart (a container-local file would not); tree 2 never opens a pull request and the checkpoint removes the file (cleanup trap on abort).
findings.finding: AC2's negative control rests on a workspace .omp/config.yml never measured in a pod

findings.answer: The daemon never refuses a ready for its report: unknown row names are dropped and logged, missing rows render open ('not reported by this session'), details are truncated to 1024 bytes; only an undecodable body is 400 as today. Handler tests cover an unknown name, a missing row and an over-long detail.
findings.finding: A 400 on a malformed report crash-loops the pod, against 'run and report'

findings.answer: A stored report counts only while the claim is ready/working/idle and the report's incarnation equals the claim's current Locator.Incarnation; a relaunching claim contributes nothing until its new process reports. The e2e waits on claim.capabilities.incarnation == locator.incarnation.
findings.finding: What a row reads while its only reporter relaunches; whether an old generation's report still rules

findings.answer: The four rows gain Ruling dispatch://LEGION-663 (Capability.Ruling's documented meaning for a live row: the issue whose check proves it); a unit test pins every live row's ruling; recorded as spec departure 2.
findings.finding: 'each row carries its ruling' cannot hold: four live rows have no ruling

findings.answer: The existing gate is the daemon's boot gate and legion probe-image over the plugin manifest (bootgate.go:388-411); bumping DaemonAPIVersion and legion.daemonApiVersion to 19 together satisfies it, proved by the goldens, daemon-api-version.test.ts and stage 2's gate-refuses-another-contract row; no plugin-side gate is added, and an 18-daemon never runs a 19-image because the image probe refuses it before a claim runs.
findings.finding: AC3 names a plugin-side gate that does not exist for worker claims

findings.answer: Every workflow claim reports under either runtime (a pane's gh reads <state_dir>/secrets/<claim>-gh, its dispatch is the plugin's); the controller session (operator's machine or daemon-launched pod) sends none; subagent sessions already skip the boot. Stage 2 asserts nothing about capabilities; its rig would show open rows in the log, harmlessly.
findings.finding: Which sessions report: tmux panes, the daemon-launched controller pod, subagents

findings.answer: The controller reads the session and the fact from read_state's row detail and reports it in the day's report, taking no other action; no capabilities.decided line exists for a live row (config.go keeps refusing it); SKILL.md, outbox.go's comment and docs/kubernetes.md change together. Named to the architect as a concern.
findings.finding: A live open row changes what openCapabilities means to the controller

findings.answer: Kept as the spec words it (open when one does), bounded by liveness: a stuck row retires when that process relaunches or its claim leaves ready/working/idle; the per-claim view and the detail name the culprit. Listed under concerns for the architect.
findings.finding: A deployment-wide row judged by any failing pod has no bound and no owner

findings.answer: The latest reports live in supervision memory (loaded once at boot, written by the ready handler's hook, persisted alongside); deployment() stays a pure memory read, so neither the tick nor the state route touches the store.
findings.finding: openCapabilities() would read the store inside the tick's open transaction with no ctx

findings.answer: ClaimView.capabilities carries {measuredAt, incarnation, ok: [names], open: [{name, detail}]}: prose only for failing rows; the full details go to the daemon's info log line, which the e2e reads for tree 2's planner.
findings.finding: Per-claim capability rows bloat the controller's read_state

findings.answer: The checkpoint keeps the markers and gains the sentence that the MCP markers may come from the session's own connection or the probe's; the planner's mcp report (both fixture servers connected) is the MCP evidence. The second-client tradeoff is documented in docs/kubernetes.md and pi-legion's CHANGELOG; a server refusing a second client reads open with its error.
findings.finding: The MCP probe's connection writes the marker the repository-configuration checkpoint reads

findings.answer: The rows are end to end by their words; an outage reads open for sessions that booted during it and heals at the next boot (a concern for the architect). The Envoy half is the ten tools' registration; reach is proved by the boot's role claim, whose failure exits the process as today.
findings.finding: Two checks measure a remote service; the Envoy half can never fail

findings.answer: Deliberate: every pod runs the one image, so a pod that cannot resolve any prompt agent is a gap wherever it sits; the detail names the unresolved agents. Listed as a concern.
findings.finding: promptAgents is the union of every role's prompts

findings.answer: The summary becomes 'reaches Dispatch through the dispatch command and Envoy through the pi-envoy tools'; the row name stays; spec departure 1.
findings.finding: The dispatch-envoy-tools row's summary still says 'tools' for Dispatch

workflowRecommendation: One implementer, tasks 0-7 in the plan's order: capabilities table and rendering first (Go, pure), then wire types and the ready/register handlers, then store + supervision, then the contract renumber with regenerated goldens (go test ./internal/api/ -update and ./internal/projection/ -update), then the extension (measurement module, claim-session, daemon-client, host typings), then docs/skills, then Stage 4b (fixture MCP server, full-agent, full-agent-negative, README). The four suite commands once at the end. A pod has no Postgres, cluster or tmux: the api/store tests run in CI, and the Stage 4b run at the head's image (STAGE4B_UNTIL=full-agent-negative) is queued by the architect through the coordinator session; the implementer's own proof is a scratch omp --mode rpc session with the built plugin against a stand-in daemon, as the plan's proof paragraph says.
